teams.heading: Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi dies in Japan after suspected training heatstroke
teams.body: The Fijian rugby community is mourning the tragic death of Saimoni Vunilagi, aged 26, who passed away in Japan on Friday. His club, second-division side Kyuden Voltex, confirmed the former Tokyo Sungoliath back-rower was hospitalised on Monday after showing severe symptoms of heatstroke following team practice in Fukuoka, where temperatures reached 35 degrees. Despite the best efforts of medical staff, Vunilagi could not be saved. The forward, who began his professional career in 2023, had only recently joined Kyushu KV in July.

lead.why: The tragic passing of 26-year-old Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi in Japan is the most significant and widely reported story today.

teams.heading: Eddie Hearn demands Northampton Saints make Henry Pollock a seven-figure player
teams.body: Negotiations between Northampton Saints and Henry Pollock remain at an impasse following Eddie Hearn’s demand for a £1m annual salary. Hearn, representing the 21-year-old flanker, insists the England starlet should become the Premiership’s first seven-figure player to ensure his long-term future at Franklin’s Gardens. While some analysts have labelled the valuation as "laudable but laughable" for a player who was sin-binned during the recent victory in Santiago, the pressure on Saints to secure their breakout talent is mounting.

teams.heading: Ion Neculai joins Northampton Saints after departing Italian club Zebre Parma
teams.body: Italian international tight-head prop Ion Neculai has signed for Northampton Saints. The 25-year-old makes the move to the Premiership champions following a five-season stint at Zebre Parma, where he totalled 51 appearances. Neculai, who holds four senior Italy caps, featured for the Azzurri as recently as last month’s Nations Championship fixture against Australia. Saints director of rugby Phil Dowson described the forward as a "very physical prop who enjoys the tough side of the game."

teams.heading: Sione Fukofuka steps down as Scotland Women head coach citing stress
teams.body: Sione Fukofuka has resigned as Scotland Women’s head coach, citing the "stress and the strain" of being separated from his family in Australia. Fukofuka, who led the side through the 2026 Six Nations, confirmed that he requested a release from his contract on compassionate grounds. Forwards coach Dave Butcher has been appointed as interim head coach as the squad prepares for the upcoming Vodafone Scotland WXV series, with squad training scheduled to begin at Oriam this Monday.

lead.why: The head coach of the women's national team has resigned, marking a significant leadership change ahead of the WXV series.

teams.body: Wales have returned to the top 10 of the World Rugby rankings for the first time since July 2024. Despite a difficult recent result against South Africa, Wales climbed one spot to 10th following Australia’s narrow victory over Japan in Osaka. This shift in the global standings sees Japan drop two places, allowing Wales to edge ahead of Italy as they continue their preparations for the upcoming autumn campaign.

teams.heading: Los Pumas fall to Springboks after Benjamin Grondona scores opening try
teams.body: Argentina produced a formidable display on Saturday, but ultimately fell 17-10 to the world champion Springboks at Vélez. Los Pumas dictated the tempo early, with Benjamin Grondona powering over in the 10th minute following a dominant opening period. Despite aggressive line speed and constant pressure at the breakdown that disrupted South African rhythm, the visitors’ bench proved decisive in the final quarter. The defeat concludes a challenging week for Felipe Contepomi’s side following disciplinary issues surrounding the squad’s recent officiating concerns.

teams.heading: Les Kiss guides Australia to narrow victory over Japan in Osaka
teams.body: The Les Kiss era began with a hard-fought 35-32 victory over Japan on Saturday, as the Wallabies survived a second-half deficit and a red card. Miles Amatosero was sent off for a high tackle on Warner Dearns, forcing the visitors to play with 14 men for a 20-minute period. Despite the pressure, tries from Harry Potter, Tom Wright, Max Jorgensen, Fraser McReight and Taniela Tupou secured the win. Kiss noted, “Smooth waters at the moment. They can get rough at any time.”

teams.body: The Brave Blossoms fell 35-32 to Australia in a dramatic Lipovitan D Challenge Cup clash on Saturday. Despite a strong performance that capitalised on an early red card for Australian lock Miles Amatosero, Japan could not overcome the visitors’ physicality in the sweltering Osaka heat. Ryunosuke Ito, Faulua Makisi, Kazuma Ueda, and captain Warner Dearns crossed for Japan, but the home side ultimately came up just short in the dying minutes of a competitive, high-tempo international fixture.
